findings.problem: Both proofs show that `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra X` lies in a closed star subalgebra by the same four-step recipe. They unfold the topological closure with `topologicalClosure_minimal`, reduce to the adjoin with `adjoin_le`, destructure the range of the entry map with `rintro _ ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩`, and then supply a closedness proof. Only the target subalgebra differs: `P.toStarSubalgebra` in the first, `StarSubalgebra.centralizer ℂ {q}` in the second. The recipe is written out twice in this file, and any change to how the algebra is defined (for example the index set) has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one minimality lemma next to `matrix_entry_mem_test_algebra`:

theorem finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_le_of_closed {n : ℕ} (X : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) (S : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hS : IsClosed (S : Set (H →L[ℂ] H))) (hX : ∀ i j, X i j ∈ S) : finiteMatrixTestAlgebra X ≤ S := by
  refine StarSubalgebra.topologicalClosure_minimal (StarAlgebra.adjoin_le ?_) hS
  rintro _ ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩
  exact hX i j

Then `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_le` becomes `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_le_of_closed X P.toStarSubalgebra (by change IsClosed P.carrier; rw [← P.centralizer_centralizer']; exact Set.isClosed_centralizer _) hX`. In `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_invariant`, `hle` becomes `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_le_of_closed X _ (Set.isClosed_centralizer _) (fun i j => (StarSubalgebra.mem_centralizer_iff ℂ).mpr (by intro g hg; obtain rfl := Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hg; exact ⟨(hX i j).eq, by simpa only [hqstar] using (hX i j).eq⟩))`. This works under the file's imports and hypotheses, since the lemma uses only `StarSubalgebra.topologicalClosure_minimal` and `StarAlgebra.adjoin_le`, which both existing proofs already use.
findings.benefit: The adjoin/closure unfolding is stated once. Each use then contains only its own mathematical content: for the von Neumann algebra, closedness of a double centralizer; for the invariant subspace, commutation with the projection `q`. This removes the repeated destructuring and makes the dependence on the definition of `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra` easier to maintain.
